title: Platform systems & services — team wiki, runbooks, dashboards and roadmap (Q3 2026 retrospective)
author: Priya Shah
body:
Summary

This page consolidates the platform team’s canonical systems & services documentation: the team wiki structure, runbooks, dashboards and alerts configuration, SLOs, recent runbook changes, and roadmap items. It includes a short retrospective covering Q3 2026 operational incidents and improvements we implemented. Use this page as the primary entry point for on-call triage, runbook edits, and quarterly planning.

Contents
1) Intro and ownership
2) Team wiki structure and contributor conventions
3) Runbooks (canonical list + quick access)
4) Dashboards & alerts (key panels and thresholds)
5) SLOs and error budgets
6) On-call triage checklist (runbook excerpt)
7) Q3 2026 retrospective & follow-ups
8) Roadmap (next 90 days)
9) How-to: adding a new dashboard or runbook
10) Appendices & links

---

1) Intro and ownership

Purpose: Provide a single, curated entry point for platform systems and services operational knowledge. This page is maintained by the Platform Systems & Services team; it documents the state of runbooks, dashboards, alerts, and short-term roadmap items that affect operational readiness.

Primary owners
- Document owner: Priya Shah (platform-systems)
- On-call rotations: platform on-call (see team wiki for schedule)
- Dashboard steward: Marco Nguyen
- Alerting steward: Sofia Alvarez

Contribution model
- All runbook changes must be submitted as PRs against the confluence content repo and include: what changed, rationale, test steps, and at least one reviewer.
- Emergency edits (during incidents) must be followed by a post-incident PR that documents the emergency change.

---

2) Team wiki structure and contributor conventions

Top-level pages (and where to find them)
- platform-team-wiki: landing page with links to systems/services, runbooks, dashboards, and roadmap.
- systems-and-services: canonical list of services (inference-api, router, batch-worker, cache-proxy, metrics-collector, alert-dispatcher).
- runbooks: folders by service, shortname-runbook.json pages.
- dashboards: folder with dashboard JSON and a README that lists panel owners and update cadence.
- retrospectives: chronological list of postmortems and quarterly retros.

Markdown / Confluence style rules
- Use headings for sections; keep prose concise.
- Include an "Owner" and "Last updated" line at the top of each runbook.
- Use numbered step sequences for triage procedures, and bullet lists for checks.
- Attach a quick CLI cheatsheet where appropriate (kubectl, grpcurl, curl examples).

Change log practice
- Add a short changelog section at bottom of each page with date, author, and summary.

---

3) Runbooks (canonical list + quick access)

Canonical runbooks (location: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/):
- inference-api-runbook.json — primary service for hosted inference endpoints. Owner: inference-service.
- router-failover-runbook.json — routing failover and degraded-mode instructions. Owner: network-team.
- cache-proxy-runbook.json — KV cache eviction and warmup. Owner: runtime-team.
- batch-worker-runbook.json — backfilling and job retry patterns. Owner: batch-team.
- metrics-collector-runbook.json — metrics pipeline backpressure and storage GC. Owner: observability-team.

Quick access: Important sections inside each runbook
- Symptoms and immediate checks (top 3): CPU/GPU utilization, error spike, queue depth.
- Mitigation steps (first 15 minutes): scale up replicas, enable degraded routing, and increase retry windows.
- Escalation matrix: who to call at 30/60/120 minutes.

Sample runbook excerpt (inference-api)
1. Verify incident scope: run `kubectl get pods -l app=inference-api -o wide` and check replica status.
2. Check p99 latency and error-rate on the inference-api dashboard (panel: inference-api latency & errors).
3. If p95 > 200ms or error rate > 1% for 3m, open incident and tag #platform-oncall.
4. If pod restart loop observed, capture logs: `kubectl logs --previous` and upload to incident channel.
5. If CPU or GPU saturation, scale the deployment (see autoscaling playbook).

---

4) Dashboards & alerts (key panels and thresholds)

High-level dashboards
- Platform Overview (team dashboard) — health of top services, global error budget, SLO burn rate. Owner: Marco Nguyen.
- Inference API (service dashboard) — latency histogram, p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate. Owner: inference-service.
- Router & traffic (network dashboard) — routing success rate, route-fallbacks, cross-region failover. Owner: network-team.
- Batch & backlog (batch dashboard) — queue depth, job throughput, retry rate. Owner: batch-team.

Key alerting thresholds (examples)
- inference-api-p99-latency-critical: triggers when p99 latency > 250ms for 5 minutes. Severity: critical. Pager: platform on-call.
- inference-api-error-rate-warning: triggers when error rate > 0.5% for 10 minutes. Severity: warning. Pager: platform SLACK alert (no pager).
- metrics-collector-dropped-metrics: triggers when metric ingestion drops > 5% relative to baseline for 3m. Severity: critical. Pager: observability on-call.

Alert routing policy
- Use three severity tiers: critical (page), major (Slack + email), minor (ticket).
- Attach runbook link in the alert payload and include the top-3 diagnostic queries.

Dashboard maintenance
- Dashboard owner is responsible for quarterly review. Update panel queries to match schema changes. Document changes in dashboard README.

---

5) SLOs and error budgets

Current service SLOs (summary table)
| Service | SLO (availability) | p99 latency SLO |
| inference-api | 99.9% successful responses 5xx/4xx below 0.1% | p99 < 200ms |
| router | 99.95% request routing success | N/A |
| metrics-collector | 99.5% ingestion within 30s | N/A |

Error budgets and burn policy
- Error budget window: 30 days for hosted API services.
- If burn rate > 2x for 12h, pause risky deploys and start rollback plan.
- If error budget exhaustion is projected within 7 days, schedule dedicated war room and full-scale mitigation.

---

6) On-call triage checklist (runbook excerpt)
1. Acknowledge the page and confirm scope in Slack.
2. Check platform overview dashboard: identify impacted services and dependent services.
3. Run quick health checks: `kubectl`, `gcloud`, `nvidia-smi` for GPU nodes, and `curl` health endpoints.
4. Apply mitigation: scale, route away, or enable degraded mode.
5. If mitigation stabilizes, document temporary fix and assign follow-up ticket.
6. If not stabilized in 30 minutes, escalate to senior on-call and open a postmortem placeholder.

Communication templates
- Incident Slack intro: short template with time, scope, impact, initial mitigation, P0 owner. Keep the first message under 5 lines.

---

7) Q3 2026 retrospective & follow-ups

Incidents summary (Q3 2026)
- 2026-07-06: Inference p99 spike caused by new tokenizer change in model-v2. Root cause: tokenization output length increase causing batcher tail latency. Impact: 45m of increased p99 across hosted API (~2.6% of traffic saw degraded latency).
- 2026-08-12: Metrics ingestion throttling after config roll in metrics-collector. Root cause: retention job misconfiguration. Impact: 2 hours of missing metrics for lower-priority customers.
- 2026-09-03: Router partial outage due to config propagation bug. Root cause: inconsistent config between regions. Impact: cross-region fallback triggered for 30 minutes.

What we shipped after those incidents
- Tokenizer change gate: new model onboarding checklist includes tokenization regression tests and a synthetic traffic run at 10x baseline before rollout. (Owner: model-onboarding).
- Batcher tail mitigation: implemented configurable max-batch-latency and per-model fast-path quantization. (Owner: serving-runtime).
- Metrics collector safe-guard: retention job now requires a dry-run and two approvers for production changes. (Owner: observability-team).
- Config propagation validation: added cross-region config checksum and a canary propagation step. (Owner: network-team).

Open follow-ups (with owners and ETA)
- Improve synthetic traffic harness to emulate long-tail token sequences (Owner: applied-ml; ETA: 2026-10-15).
- Add an automated runbook-validation tool that runs smoke checks after runbook edits (Owner: eng-developer-experience; ETA: 2026-11-01).
- Expand dashboard retention window for critical latency panels to 90 days for seasonal analysis (Owner: observability-team; ETA: 2026-10-01).

Retrospective notes (lessons learned)
- Validate model-level changes (tokenizers, output length) at serving scale before traffic ramp.
- Treat config propagation as first-class traffic: add checksum and canary policies.
- Make runbooks executable where possible: include CLI snippets and quick-check scripts.

---

8) Roadmap (next 90 days)

Planned work (high level)
- Runbook automation: wire runbooks to a small set of automated responders for common mitigations (auto-scale, toggle degraded routing). Owner: eng-platform. ETA: 2026-11-15.
- Dashboard & alerting audit: complete review of all platform alerts to reduce noise by 30%. Owner: observability-team. ETA: 2026-10-30.
- Improved onboarding checklist for Private deployments: include network/security test harness and audit logging validation. Owner: eng-private-deployments. ETA: 2026-12-01.
- Post-incident drill schedule: monthly tabletop exercises for top 3 failure modes. Owner: eng-sre. ETA: start 2026-10-01.

Dependencies & risks
- Automation requires changes to alerting service RBAC (risk: misplaced automation could cause noisy actions). Mitigation: staged rollout and kill-switch.
- Dashboard audit requires adequate time from service owners; schedule with product leads.

---

9) How-to: adding a new dashboard or runbook (step-by-step)

Add a dashboard
1. Create a panel JSON in /dashboards/drafts with owner metadata.
2. Add test queries and a short description of signal intent.
3. Request review from Dashboard Steward (Marco Nguyen).
4. After review, move to /dashboards/ and tag in the quarterly review doc.

Add/edit a runbook
1. Fork the runbook file and add your change with a clear changelog entry.
2. Add or update the "Owner" and "Last updated" fields.
3. Include at least one reproducible quick-check command and expected outputs.
4. Open PR and request review from owner and one reviewer.
5. Once merged, notify on #platform-docs and schedule a short walkthrough if the change is substantial.

Runbook validation checklist (before merge)
- Has owner approved?
- Do CLI checks work in staging?
- Is there a rollback/undo step documented?
